process_type: self-terminating atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) and layer-by-layer
temperature_range: Below 120 °C for amorphous films; 250-350 °C for single-crystal films
summary: The study describes the epitaxial growth of GaN on (0001) SiC substrates using a self-terminating atomic layer epitaxy (ALE) method combined with a layer-by-layer technique and a novel reactor design with hot filaments to decompose ammonia. The process was optimized to achieve single-crystal GaN films at temperatures above 250-350 °C, with amorphous films formed at lower temperatures. The growth was influenced by temperature, exposure time, and the use of heated filaments to enhance surface mobility and decomposition of precursor gases.
evidence: GaN films have been grown on (0001)SiC substrates from triethylgallium and ammonia sources using a self-terminating atomic layer epitaxy method, as well as a layer-by-layer technique and a novel reactor design employing hot filaments to decompose the ammonia. The material properties and growth process were strongly dependent on the temperature and exposure time. GaN grew in a self-terminating fashion for temperatures below 120 °C but the films were amorphous. Above this temperature, the films were deposited in a layer-by-layer process giving single-crystal material in the 250-350 °C range.
